sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Calcium mobilisation assay (Gα15 coupling): in vitro potency and efficacy of HA-tagged rat mGlu7 were determined and reported as functional; tag did not abolish receptor activity.
sites.rationale: GRM7 has a single extracellular N-terminus (residues 35–590, the large Venus Flytrap/CRD ectodomain) and an intracellular C-terminus; the only extracellular terminus for a prepended tag is after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 34. Python lookup confirms residue 34 = G and residue 35 = Q in the canonical gapped numbering. L1 (rat mGlu7, HA, functional calcium assay) is used as primary because it provides the highest validation level; L2 (mGlu7a, extracellular c-myc, HEK293T) and L4 (human mGluR7, ALFA tag replacing endogenous SP) independently corroborate the identical junction. The insert site is >550 residues from the first TM helix (sequential boundary 591), satisfying the ≥3-residue TM-distance constraint, and N-terminal tagging of mGluRs is a well-established approach that does not perturb ligand binding or G-protein coupling. Full-length rat mGlu7 N-terminally tagged with HA epitope; split Renilla Luciferase 8 fragments fused to C-terminus; expressed in cells and used in calcium mobilisation assays via Gα15. Rat mGlu7 is a close ortholog of human mGluR7 (GRM7). The same N-terminal extracellular junction is independently supported by L2 (extracellular c-myc-tagged mGlu7a in HEK293T) and L4 (human mGluR7 with endogenous SP replaced by HA-SP + ALFA tag, placing ALFA at the identical mature N-terminus). No residue number is named in any of the three clips; the junction is derived from the single extracellular terminus: the tag must follow the cleaved signal peptide, placing it after residue 34 (last SP residue, G) and before residue 35 (Q, first residue of the mature VFT domain).

sources.claim:
Calcium assays in which rat mGlu 7 was coupled to calcium mobilization via the promiscuous G protein G α15 were used to determine in vitro potency and efficacy and were conducted as described in ( 18 , 26 , 41 , 42 , 43 ).
cDNAs for rat mGlu 7 and mGlu 8 were N-terminally tagged with a hemagglutinin epitope tag using standard molecular biology procedures. cDNAs encoding the split fragments of Renilla Luciferase 8, L1 (residues 1–229), or L2 (residues 230–311), were fused in frame to the C-terminus of mGlu 7 and mGlu 8 following the linker “GSPPARAT” in the pcDNA3.1 vector.

literature_notes: L1, L2, and L4 all pin the same junction (insert_after_residue=34, after signal-peptide cleavage) and therefore constitute one site; L1 was chosen as primary because it provides functional validation (calcium assay). L4 (human mGluR7, ALFA tag) is the most directly task-relevant clip and independently confirms the same junction on the human protein. L3 describes a C-terminal eGFP/Flag/His10 fusion on a truncated human mGluR7 construct (sequential residues 1–859); sequential position 859 maps to gapped position 863, which falls within the intracellular C-terminal domain (sequential 851–915), so this is recorded in other_positions rather than sites.

literature_other_positions.note: eGFP, Flag, and His10 tags fused via HRV-3C site to the C-terminus of a truncated human mGluR7 construct (sequential residues 1–859; gapped position 863); sequential position 859 lies within the intracellular C-terminal domain (sequential 851–915), so this tag faces the cytoplasm and is not a surface-accessible site.
